validity.recommendation: UNRESOLVED — flag for a human with Moldovan-source access rather than editing LengthKnownKm. Do not adopt 166 km as a replacement value; do not assume 44 km is wrong without a source stating what it counts.
validity.researcher_notes:
The drawn geodesic (166 km) exceeds the stated LengthKnownKm (44 km) by a factor of 3.77, and per gotcha 3 this is the direction that IS evidence of a real disagreement (a drawn span far exceeding the stated length, not the reverse). My own rough coordinate check (Odesa ~46.48N/30.72E to Chisinau ~47.02N/28.86E) puts the great-circle distance at roughly 150-165 km, i.e. the 166 km drawn route is closely consistent with a line running the FULL stated endpoints Odesa-Chisinau, which raises the question of what the 44 km actually measures.

What I checked and could not resolve: (1) Moldovatransgaz's own site via the mtg.md mirror (gotcha 2 — moldovatransgaz.md fails TLS, mtg.md verifies 200) gives only aggregate network figures (1,560 km of transport pipeline across Moldova, 3 linear production sectors at Chisinau/Drochia/Vulcanesti) and names one specific line, the Ananiev-Cernauti-Bogorodceni (ACB) trunk — an unrelated northern/western corridor, not this one — with no asset-level length table that would let me place a 44 km or 166 km segment. (2) Vestmoldtransgaz (the entity that would plausibly operate a Ukraine-Moldova cross-border interconnector, distinct from Moldovatransgaz's domestic network) — vestmoldtransgaz.md does not resolve (connection error, checked both with and without www), and I found no working alternate URL for it. (3) ANRE Moldova's natural-gas section (anre.md/gaze-naturale) 404s; I did not find the current URL for their network/interconnection-point documentation in the time available. (4) English/Ukrainian/Romanian Wikipedia have no dedicated article on this pipeline (confirmed via a Wikipedia full-text search, which returned only unrelated Moldova-energy-crisis and Iasi-Chisinau-pipeline hits — a distinct, much newer, Romania-sourced line commissioned 2021-2023, not this one). (5) utg.ua/tsoua.com were not chased for this specific point since the corporate-history pages that might document a cross-border interconnector's own commissioning specs are unlikely to carry a Moldovan asset's length figure even via Wayback.

My best working hypothesis, NOT proposed as a fill: 44 km may represent only the Ukrainian-side spur (Odesa to the border/metering point) rather than the full cross-border run to Chisinau, given the sheet's Owner is listed as 'Moldovatransgaz [100.%]' — a Moldovan state operator owning 100% of a line whose StartCountryOrArea is Ukraine is itself slightly unusual and worth a human look alongside the length question; it is consistent with either (a) GEM's own length capturing only a partial/metered segment while the geometry was drawn for the whole named corridor, or (b) the Owner attribution being the actual defect. I am not confident enough in either to propose a value change.
